title: When the Bell Is Tolled
subtitle: Now, the high hanging sword has fallen.

items.text: When the Bell Is Tolled
The monastery was crowded far beyond its usual numbers.
But those that had gathered there came neither for prayer nor to celebrate a holy day.

items.speaker: Monk
items.text: My Lady, I received no notice from the abbot. Were your actions sanctioned through the proper channels?

items.speaker: Monk
items.text: To gather such a large number of the faithful here, we need some authorized reason.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Those gathered here are not just the faithful of your monastery.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: They are perpetrators and victims both, trapped by rumors and prejudice.

items.speaker: Monk
items.text: But...

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: We will proceed with the trial immediately.
Dikke walked straight to the altar, and the hushed conversations below her fell into a fearful silence.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Chester, a brother of this monastery is dead, I stand here to contend that he was killed, and I shall preside as the prosecutor of this case.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: The accused is—

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: —everyone present.
Dikke's voice wasn't loud, more like a sword raised slowly before an execution.
Her words echoed between the monastery's gray walls and stained-glass windows, a distant thunder in the ears of the gathered crowd.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Let us present the first witness.

items.speaker: Civilian I
items.text: My Lady, you promised to protect us!

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: I am here now, protecting you, am I not?

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Protecting innocent people plagued by fear and rumors.
She glanced coldly over the crowd, subduing countless pairs of terrified eyes.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: You believed he was a ghoul.

items.speaker: Civilian I
items.text: That's what the rumors said... We came to warn him, that's all.

items.speaker: Civilian I
items.text: They... They all said so...

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Your claim is that you had a simple argument with the deceased, "only advising him against wandering around the cemetery with wild notions," is that so?

items.speaker: Civilian I
items.text: ...Yes, that's right.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Yet the deceased doesn't appear to agree with your version of these events.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Now I will call for the second witness.
A withered corpse was presented. To the shock and horror of those assembled.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: Lady Dikke, you have committed a grave sin! To desecrate our brother's corpse like this ... this ...

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: This is a serious violation!

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Your concerns are noted.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Yet my actions strictly follow the methods described in Brother Chester's "Mysteries of the Human Body".

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Which I undertook to honor him.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: You're desecrating the corpse...

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: I must report this to the authorities immediately!

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: My lady, forgive us.
Her actions were decisive, just like everything she did.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: The trial will proceed.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Observe on the deceased here multiple blunt force injuries, skin lacerations, and at the wound sites, remains of soil and dry grass.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Do you plead guilty?

items.speaker: Civilian I
items.text: I confess, we did hit him... but he didn't die! We saw him rise from his fall alive.

items.speaker: Civilian I
items.text: When we confronted him, he was in the midst of moving a body! He's a ghoul, just as the rumors claimed!

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: And yet, my trial continues.
The priest trembled on his feet, closing his eyes and muttering desperate prayers of forgiveness.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: Dear God, forgive me...

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Now, I turn to you, Father Malachi.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: On this night, was your meeting with Brother Chester in the tower mere happenstance?

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Or was it a planned encounter?
Sharp and incisive, Dikke swiftly honed herself upon the latest of her accused.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: He ... had invited me to discuss an important matter ...

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: He wanted you to mobilize everyone in the monastery to copy the guide he had written and spread it to all our followers—he claimed to be bringing a revelation to the people ...

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: My Lord, how could I trust the words of such a wizard, especially when he stood to blame us for our previous inaction during the great plague?!
His legs were trembling, teeth tightly clenched.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: So it was that you refused his request yet still took the wine he offered.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: It was a gift...

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: What he said was hard to believe... I simply gave him a test!

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: Were he truly a capable wizard, he should have easily been able to remove the dust from the clock on the roof of the building, right?

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: So he fell to his death.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: And you went back to drinking, as usual, in "moderation".

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: Please... please forgive me...
The dark cloaked lady ascended to the highest point in the room.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: I will now pronounce judgment.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: This was a silent murder to which all are guilty.
TO BE CONTINUED…
